_comment: Copy to params-external-volume.json and fill in. That file is gitignored.
_what_this_is: Backing store for Snowflake Managed Iceberg Tables. Separate from params.example.json, which configures read access to an FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Point.
_setup: scripts/setup_external_volume.sh --bucket <your-bucket> walks through the three phases and prints the SQL.
_BucketName_help: Globally unique across all of AWS. Include your org and region, e.g. acme-lakehouse-iceberg-apne1. This is a STANDARD S3 bucket, not the Access Point - Iceberg writes to an Access Point are not usable (BLK-002, BLK-009).
_BucketPrefix_help: Keep the trailing slash. Snowflake creates one folder per table underneath.
_CreateBucket_help: true to create it here. false if it already exists or another team owns it.
_phase_note: Leave the next two empty on the first deploy. Snowflake only issues them after CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME, so the trust policy cannot be correct until phase 3.
_SnowflakeIamUserArn_help: STORAGE_AWS_IAM_USER_ARN from DESC EXTERNAL VOLUME. An IAM *user* ARN in a Snowflake-owned account - if what you copied contains ':role/', you copied the wrong field.
_SnowflakeExternalId_help: STORAGE_AWS_EXTERNAL_ID from DESC EXTERNAL VOLUME. Looks like ACCOUNT_SFCRole=2_base64string= and ends with '='. Truncating it is the most common cause of Access Denied.
_outputs_comment: Filled in by the setup script after deployment. Not inputs.
